answer: Bond depreciation is a parking meter that never stops. An identity buys a 120-unit bond, locked for 10 epochs, losing 4% of face value each epoch. Fall below 60 and the identity is downgraded and loses its rights. Only real work tops the bond back to face value. A nebula of idle bonds fades every epoch, a falcon cannot speed the meter, and the juniper of stored value dries out. Cheating forfeits 50% of the remainder and freezes top-ups for 6 epochs. Buying 1,000 bonds costs 120,000 units. Each epoch burns 4,800 units; 10 idle epochs lose over 40,000.
